page.overview:
Who is Adam Clay?

Adam Clay lived with his Australian parents on a plantation in Burma. During World War II the Japanese invaded the country before Clay's family could get out. Only Adam Clay escaped on his family's crop duster and the death of his family changed him, but it also made him strong.

He founded a group of disenfranchised fliers from around the world like himself affected by the Axis and formed a private air corps.

Due to Adam's Australian background and most especially after the team's planes, with their distinctive V-wing formation, he adopted the nickname Captain Boomerang. Clay and his corps fought throughout World War II and had other fantastic adventures.

After fighting other wars in the fight for freedom, Clay stayed young from genetic surgery thus never having to retire or stand down as leader. During the 1960s, Clay had a lover, reporter Michelle Curry, and wanted to propose to her. Though Michelle wanted her independence and she couldn't decide. Unknown to Clay, he impregnated Michelle in which she later gave birth to their son Arthur. After Michelle's pregnancy, she decided to accept Clay's marriage and planned to announce her decision to him via a letter while she was serving as a war correspondent in the 1968 Czechoslovakian war. S. Army base in Pilsen. Years later, Clay fatefully first met his biological son during the midst of an attack from a team of aerial villains called the Darkstars. After having dealt with the Darkstars in which Arthur also helped the Boomerangs, Clay was left impressed with Arthur's actions and accepted him in joining his corps.

entity.description:
Adam Clay lived with his Australian parents on a plantation in Burma. During World War II the Japanese invaded the country before Clay's family could get out. Only Adam Clay escaped on his family's crop duster and the death of his family changed him, but it also made him strong. He founded a group of disenfranchised fliers from around the world like himself affected by the Axis and formed a private air corps. Due to Adam's Australian background and most especially after the team's planes, with their distinctive V-wing formation, he adopted the nickname Captain Boomerang. Clay and his corps fought throughout World War II and had other fantastic adventures. After fighting other wars in the fight for freedom, Clay stayed young from genetic surgery thus never having to retire or stand down as leader.

During the 1960s, Clay had a lover, reporter Michelle Curry, and wanted to propose to her. Though Michelle wanted her independence and she couldn't decide. Unknown to Clay, he impregnated Michelle in which she later gave birth to their son Arthur. After Michelle's pregnancy, she decided to accept Clay's marriage and planned to announce her decision to him via a letter while she was serving as a war correspondent in the 1968 Czechoslovakian war. But tragically, Michelle was unable to send the letter as she was killed in the bombing of the U.S. Army base in Pilsen.

Years later, Clay fatefully first met his biological son during the midst of an attack from a team of aerial villains called the Darkstars. After having dealt with the Darkstars in which Arthur also helped the Boomerangs, Clay was left impressed with Arthur's actions and accepted him in joining his corps.
